clue.text: An antique cabinet?

parts.note: a cabinet here is a governing body rather than furniture, and antique means made up of the elderly

explanation.surface: A dealer's question about an old piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests a cupboard in an antiques shop; read it as a group of ministers who are all old.
explanation.definitionFit: Government by old people is a ruling body of elders, a cabinet that is aged.

clue.text: Rough increased round middle of fairway

indicators.note: the word for increased is placed round the other piece

parts.note: to have increased is to have gained

indicators.note: the central letter of the seven-letter word fairway is taken

explanation.surface: A golfer notes the rough has grown around the centre of the fairway.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood or stone with a coarse texture is described as rough-surfaced, with visible grain.

clue.text: Unusual, unfinished pole dance

parts.note: rum is an old word for odd or unusual

indicators.note: the word for pole loses its final letter

parts.note: a bar is a pole or rod

explanation.surface: An odd, incomplete pole-dancing routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance with a lively rhythm.

clue.text: Sudden flow under the bridge?

parts.note: the bridge is that of the nose, and the flow under it is of blood

explanation.surface: A river rising suddenly beneath a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge is not over a river but the bony ridge at the top of the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood streaming from the nostrils is a sudden flow beneath the nasal bridge.

clue.text: Initially old body in tomb may get this

definitions.text: Initially old body in tomb may get this

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next four words are taken

explanation.surface: An old corpse laid to rest earns a write-up in the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A death notice in a newspaper is what an old body going to the grave may receive.

clue.text: Chips topped with fish and white wine

indicators.note: the word for chips loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: fries is the American word for chips
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A pub meal of chips and fish washed down with a glass of white.
explanation.definitionFit: A grape variety from Germany and Alsace making aromatic white wines.

clue.text: 'Plates', mate, in rhyming slang

definitions.meaning: fine porcelain crockery such as plates
in Cockney rhyming slang a friend is a ... plate, shortened to its first word

explanation.surface: A definition of a slang term for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain tableware is so called, and Cockney rhyming slang uses 'china plate' for mate, a friend.

clue.text: With record time around edge, they don't last

indicators.note: the record and time pieces sit around the word for edge

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
an era is a period of time
a hem is the edge of cloth

explanation.surface: Something about a record and a time limit, then things that are short-lived.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-lived things, especially printed items such as tickets and posters not meant to be kept.

clue.text: Cleo half dispatched by snake's embraces

indicators.note: half of the name Cleo is sent away, leaving its first two letters

parts.note: an asp is a snake, and the 's adds the S

explanation.surface: Cleopatra half killed by the asp, as legend has it.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleopatra died by an asp's bite; the shortened name Cleo makes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp someone is to hold them tightly, so the noun plural means hugs or embraces.

clue.text: Peace, it's arranged with Crimea in turmoil

indicators.note: arranged means set into a new order, so these letters are rearranged
turmoil throws the letters of the peninsula's name into disorder too

explanation.surface: A truce agreed while Crimea is in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce or ceasefire agreed between warring sides brings peace.

clue.text: Stimulate beginner after setter's exercise

indicators.note: the beginner's letter comes after the other two pieces

parts.note: the setter is 'I', and setter's is I'm, I am
PE is physical education
L is the learner plate's letter

explanation.surface: A setter's workout encouraging a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive or urge someone forward is to stimulate them into action.

clue.text: Close almost bowled for fifty

indicators.note: one letter goes in for another, the bowled one replacing the fifty

parts.note: nearly means almost
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A batsman almost reaches fifty before being bowled, a close thing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman dismissed bowled is written B on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close by is a short distance away, a synonym.

clue.text: Sailors perhaps, catching large fish

indicators.note: the sailors' word holds the large letter inside it

parts.note: boaters are people who go boating, and also straw hats sailors wore
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Sailors hauling in a big catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloater is a herring cured whole by salting and smoking, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Provided iron in dagger case for conflict

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the dagger's case
the case of a word is its outer letters, here first and last

parts.note: if means provided that
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Iron weapons and a dagger sheath supplied for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at odds or disagree is to conflict with each other.

clue.text: Fugitive getting away with time inside…

indicators.note: the time letter is placed inside the word for getting away

parts.note: fleeing means running away

explanation.surface: A fugitive escaping while serving time, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fugitive' looks like a person on the run, but here it is the adjective meaning transient.
explanation.definitionFit: Fugitive can mean passing quickly, transient, as in a fugitive glimpse.

clue.text: A thousand pounds is found in pants

parts.note: K stands for a thousand
nicker is British slang for pounds sterling, unchanged in the plural
is shortened to 's gives S

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds discovered in someone's underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage pants are underpants, and this word is women's underwear.

clue.text: …imprison criminal with stretch

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
to strain is to stretch to the limit

explanation.surface: Continuing the fugitive story: lock up the criminal for a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretch' looks like slang for a prison term, but it is the verb meaning to pull taut.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine or restrict someone is to hold them as if imprisoned.

clue.text: Guard posted on border left to last

parts.note: sent means posted, as a letter

indicators.note: the left letter moves from the front of the border word to its end

parts.note: a line is a border or boundary

explanation.surface: A guard stationed on the frontier, left there till the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier standing watch is a guard or sentry.

clue.text: More fashionable line's about right design

indicators.note: the tier word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a tier is a row or line, and 's is link
an end is an aim or design

explanation.surface: A clothing line chasing the right look.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means in fashion, so the comparative means more in vogue.

clue.text: Score getting a couple of kisses

definitions.meaning: a score is a group of ...
two kisses are XX, the Roman numeral for ...

explanation.surface: Scoring and getting two kisses, a romantic success.
explanation.walkthrough: A kiss is written X, so two of them make XX, which in Roman numerals is the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, and XX is the same number in Roman numerals.

clue.text: Bats and silly point's caught

indicators.note: the silly word catches the point letter inside it

parts.note: inane means silly
S is south, a compass point; 's is is

explanation.surface: Cricket: a batsman and a fielder at silly point, who is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: Silly point is a fielding position very close to the batsman, so the cricket words all mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats is informal for crazy or mad, as in going bats.

clue.text: Oriental bird supporting endless massage

indicators.note: in a down entry the bird sits beneath the other part, supporting it
the soothing word loses its last letter

parts.note: to ease is to massage, soothe
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: An exotic bird holding up a never-ending massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental describes things from the East, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Cry wolf in account

indicators.note: the wolfing word goes inside the account word

parts.note: an entry is an item recorded in an account
to wolf food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: Crying wolf in one's story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cry wolf' looks like the idiom for false alarm; 'Cry' is the definition and 'wolf' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest plea or appeal is a cry for help.

clue.text: Planet from near the centre

indicators.note: the letters come from the centre of the phrase near the, dropping its outer letters

explanation.surface: A planet close to the middle of the solar system.
explanation.definitionFit: Our home world is the third planet from the Sun.

clue.text: Small auditory accessory, small bone

parts.note: S again for small
a cassette tape is something you listen to
S again for small

explanation.surface: A tiny hearing aid described as a small bone, fitting since the bone sits in the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The stirrup-shaped ossicle of the middle ear is the smallest bone in the human body.

clue.text: Previous conviction for religious leader

definitions.meaning: in police slang, a record of an earlier criminal sentence is called a ...
the head of a priory or deputy to an abbot in a monastery

explanation.surface: A clergyman with a criminal record.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: slang for an earlier criminal record, and the title of a monk heading a priory under an abbot.

clue.text: Shoot up for some jazz

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to dart is to shoot or dash

explanation.surface: Taking drugs to listen to jazz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot up' suggests injecting drugs; 'up' is the reversal sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional jazz, the New Orleans style revived in 1950s Britain, is a kind of jazz.

clue.text: Singer's note heard by the audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote

explanation.surface: A singer's note reaching the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks musical but is a British ten-pound banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: A male voice between baritone and alto, and so a singer of that part.

clue.text: Rodent following piper's rear in childlike story

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the childlike word

parts.note: naive means childlike, innocent

indicators.note: the rodent comes after the piper's back letter
the last letter of the piper's name is taken

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: The Pied Piper's tale of rats, a children's story.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of events, a story.

clue.text: London pride variety includes first of hardy perennial?

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters are rearranged
the opening letter of hardy is taken

explanation.surface: London pride, a saxifrage, being a hardy perennial plant.
explanation.walkthrough: London pride is a garden plant, a pink-flowered saxifrage, so the surface seems all about it. 'includes' tells you the H joins the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a popular houseplant that lives for years, so an example of a perennial, hence the question mark.
